Entry points

Where a Faber program starts.

The ordinary entry point#

main — "it begins". No parameters, no return type.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
main {
    print "Salve, munde!"
}

Async entry point#

async_main — "it will begin". Use it when the program awaits anything.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
async_main {
    print "async ready"
}

The two are alternatives, not a pair: a program declares one or the other.

Exit code#

exit (en exit) after the entry sets the process exit code. The body runs to its end first and keeps its output; the code is only the status the process returns, so exit 3 does not stop the body early. faber run ends with that code, and so does the program built for any target that runs programs: the runner, Rust, Go, TypeScript, Swift, Python, LLVM and Cranelift all end with the status the entry names. A plain entry ends with 0.

Since 1.19 the code must be in the POSIX range 0 to 255. A constant outside it is refused (SEM010 main_exit_out_of_range), and a run-time value outside it traps, on the runner and every target alike.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
main exit 2 {
    print "done"
}

Command-line arguments#

args binds the parsed argument object.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
main args args {
    print "started"
}

Naming the command#

The @ cli annotation names the binary the package produces.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
@ cli { name = "salve" }
main args args {
    print "started"
}

Declaring options#

@ option declares one command-line option. Repeat it for each. The binding name comes first, then keyword-introduced fields — no braces, no commas.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
@ cli { name = "salve" }
@ option { binding = name, short = "n", long = "nomen", type = string, description = "who to greet" }
@ option { binding = quotiens, long = "quotiens", type = int, description = "how many times" }
main args args {
    print "started"
}
FieldPurpose
(first word)The name the parsed value binds to
shortShort flag, as in -n
longLong flag, as in --nomen
typeThe option's type
descriptionHelp text
globalAccept the option on every subcommand

An option can declare long without short, as quotiens does above.

Related: Commands for running what you build, and A program is a package for the surrounding package layout.
